quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

18 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no signals, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop if you see or hear a train.
Go across the tracks as fast as you can.
Cross at your normal speed.
Go slowly across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if you see or hear a train.
questions.explanation: When there are no signals at a railroad crossing, slow down and be ready to stop if you see or hear a train coming.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle coming from the right.
The vehicle coming from the left.
The vehicle whose driver honks first.
The vehicle traveling fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control devices, you must yield to a vehicle coming from the right.

questions.question: When can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: After the train has passed.
Never.
When the lights stop flashing.
When other drivers do it.

questions.explanation: You must always stop at railroad crossings when signals warn of a train. Do not try to go around a lowered gate. These signals include flashing red lights, a gate, a flagger, or a train's horn.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Turn on your flashers.
Pull to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle's siren, pull over to the side or curb and stop.

questions.question: A driver ahead is not dimming their high beams at you. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the other vehicle.
To the right side of the road.
To the left side of the road.
Straight ahead down the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look to the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you see enough of the road to stay on course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: When a school bus stops with its stop arm out, you should:

options.text: Stop completely and wait to go.
Honk and pass on the left side.
Keep driving when children are done exiting.
Pass before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait to go.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus shows its stop signal. Do not go until the stop arm is raised.

questions.question: You may turn left on a red light if:

options.text: No traffic is coming from the other direction.
You are turning from a two-way street to a one-way street.
You are turning from a one-way street to another one-way street.
The car in front of you turns left.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are turning from a one-way street to another one-way street.
questions.explanation: You can turn left at a red light if you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street, unless a sign says you cannot. You must stop first and yield to pedestrians and other traffic.

questions.question: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning, you should drive:

options.text: Through shallow water.
Faster.
Slower.
Through deep water.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means:

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and get ready to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming next. Slow down and get ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, go through carefully.

questions.question: A car with high beams is coming toward you. You should look toward the ____ of the road.

options.text: Either side
Center
Right side
Left side

questions.explanation: Look to the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the high beams and lets you see enough to stay on course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass traffic going the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You can only cross a solid yellow line when you are turning.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign do?

options.text: Warns of hazards ahead or possible dangers.
Alerts drivers to school zones.
Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.
Alerts drivers to food and gas locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns of hazards ahead or possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers about hazards. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: What happens when you take drugs and alcohol together?

options.text: It increases the risk of a crash.
It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
It lessens the effects of alcohol.
It has no effect on your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs can affect your brain and impair your driving. Combining alcohol with drugs increases the crash risk.

questions.question: Where should your car be positioned when making a right turn?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Move as far to the right as possible before turning right. Do not cut across traffic lanes.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must you do?

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Copy what other cars are doing instead.
Assume the guard is not supposed to be there.
Follow normal traffic rules.

questions.explanation: Always follow a crossing guard's directions. Slow down and be extra careful in school zones.

questions.question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?

options.text: Whoever started moving last.
The driver.
Whoever is slower.
The pedestrian.

questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection, with or without a crosswalk.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going further.
Slow down and yield for trains.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield for trains.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down when approaching train tracks. Trains cannot yield to cars, so let them pass first.

questions.question: What should you do at a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.
